applies_when: age < 16 years for scoring (< 18 years for consent and pathway). Blueprint 9.5: NEWS2 must not be used in children aged <16 [S1].
news2_suppression_reason: NEWS2 should not be used in children (ie aged <16 years) - Royal College of Physicians [S1]. Blueprint 2.2 identifies applying it anyway as the single highest-value safety fix in Round 2.

age_bands.label: neonate <28 days
age_bands.source_note: ESI Handbook 5th edition, decision point D5: <1 mo HR >190, RR >60.

age_bands.label: 1-12 months
age_bands.source_note: ESI v5 D5: 1-12 mo HR >180, RR >55.

age_bands.label: 1-3 years
age_bands.source_note: ESI v5 D5: 1-3 y HR >140, RR >40.

age_bands.label: 3-5 years
age_bands.source_note: ESI v5 D5: 3-5 y HR >120, RR >35.

age_bands.label: 12-18 years
age_bands.source_note: ESI v5 D5: 12-18 y HR >100, RR >20. Blueprint 9.5 table B: 16-18 is DUAL-SCORED under this envelope and the adult envelope, acting on the worse result, because NEWS2 becomes valid at 16 [S1] while ESI's paediatric band runs to 18 [S5].

fever_rules.text: Fever >38 C in an infant under 28 days is at minimum a level-2 situation, regardless of how well the child looks.
fever_rules.note: Blueprint scenario S-06 exists specifically to assert a benign appearance cannot suppress this rule.

fever_rules.text: 1-3 months: consider level 2 if temperature >38 C.
>=3 months: consider level 2 or 3 if >39 C or <36 C, if immunisations are incomplete, or if there is no obvious source.

non_vital_discriminators.source_note: Mirrors the UK national paediatric early warning system scored parameter set (RCPCH / NHS England).

carer_concern_trigger.text: Parent or carer concern escalates a child's care regardless of other assessments. Imported directly from UK national PEWS practice.
carer_concern_trigger.note: Blueprint 12.2 T3: escalate-only. It can raise attention and can never lower anything.

systolic_bp.note: Blueprint 8.2 and scenario S-04: in small children capillary refill substitutes where BP is unreliable or unobtainable. Absence of BP here is 'not applicable' and carries no completeness penalty - the only reason that does.

assumptions.text: Estimated age within +/-2 years of a band boundary triggers dual-envelope evaluation, acting on the more acute result. Blueprint 9.5 table B - our rule, not anyone's guideline. Rationale: an estimated 'about 3' that is actually 2 crosses a threshold where HR >140 becomes HR >180.
Age 16-18 is dual-scored under this envelope and the adult envelope, acting on the worse result, because the two authorities disagree about where childhood ends. Blueprint 9.5 table B.
